doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Passing on professional attitude to students
summary: Butch rarely has to lecture talented students about conduct; Monk notes the life lessons from Basie are ours to pass on.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Thank you. Do you have the opportunity to try to hip your students to the kind of attitude and demeanor that they need to have to rise to the top of someone’s drummer list? Beyond their playing ability.

Every once in a while. I’ve been very fortunate enough to have some young students who have been extraordinary drummers. And I’d be lying if I said that I had to read them the riot act about how to comport themselves offstage. I haven’t, because the young gentlemen and young lady that were so excellent in their playing and when they were on the bandstand or in a concert hall or theater, they always had a wonderful attitude about everything. About the music, about people, about life. I didn’t have to say hardly a word ever. Others sometimes who have a bit of a nasty attitude generally are not your best players. Sometimes you’ll get somebody who is a great musician and is also a punk. Okay well I just don’t want to have too much to do with them and I’d rather listen to the music but I don’t want to hang around and let’s go out for dinner tomorrow night or let’s go to a movie, or like Buddy Rich once said, “Well go to a movie and hold sticks.”

Sticks, sticks, sticks. He really did say that. But there’s very few people that I’ve found that have great intelligence and talent that are real crummy people. And I’m lucky that way. I guess I don’t have to worry about it. I don’t have to think too much about it. There’s been a few times when I have sort of guided a musician, one of my students, in a way to handle a situation a little bit better than maybe they did handle it. But I also consider that to be part of the education system. That goes along with drumming, music, and just life in general. You’re here, this is university time, welcome to the university. Now you start to think for yourself. Here’s some rules, here’s some regulations. You can either use these as guidelines or you don’t have to. If you don’t I’ll probably see you some other time because you’ll wind up dropping out and getting mad and going somewhere and doing something. But most of the time, the majority of the time, the people, these youngsters are really nice people. And I don’t have to say hardly anything.

Well it sounds like you were lucky to, playing with Basie and those folks. You’ve got life lessons from them. And now, our generation is the one that’s, it’s our turn to pass them on I guess you could say.
